questions.q: What IS this feature in one sentence?
questions.a: Governs the player character's suit-based life support: O2 drain rate, temperature tolerance, health regeneration, and hazard damage per biome.

questions.q: What wider system does it belong to?
questions.a: The 9-rung compositional world model — body_survival is rung 3/9 (ground_terrain → body_survival → biome_resources).

questions.q: What would break if this feature didn't exist?
questions.a: The player would be immortal — no O2 drain, no temperature damage, no reason to seek shelter, no survival pressure that gives giving its weight.

questions.q: What existing feature does this most resemble?
questions.a: shelter_threshold (both create survival pressure that makes resource management meaningful).

questions.q: Is this a rung, a sub-rung, or a parameter?
questions.a: Rung — it's one of the 9 independently trained composition rungs.

questions.q: What physical constraint does it encode?
questions.a: O2 drains at 0.25L/s outside shelter. Temperature below -10C or above 40C causes 1HP/s damage. Shelter interior restores O2 at 2L/s and neutralizes temperature damage.

questions.q: What is the ONE measurement that proves it works?
questions.a: A player standing outside with full O2 tank (300L) survives exactly 1200 seconds before O2 depletion triggers first HP damage tick.

questions.q: What wall must it never violate?
questions.a: Must never kill the player faster than they can react (no instant-death mechanics). O2 warning must trigger at 15% remaining with audible alert.

questions.q: What would a degenerate winner look like?
questions.a: A winner with 1HP/s O2 drain (player dies in 5min with full tank) or one with 0.001L/s (player never needs to manage O2).

questions.q: How would we know if the constraint is too loose?
questions.a: If the player can survive 30+ minutes without any O2 management, the drain rate constraint is too loose to create survival pressure.

questions.q: At what scale does this feature operate?
questions.a: Per-player-instance, evaluated every tick (60fps) — O2 drain and temperature are continuous systems, not event-driven.

questions.q: What is the right definition level for this scale?
questions.a: Parameter-level: 5 float parameters (o2_drain_rate, o2_tank_capacity, temp_damage_threshold_low, temp_damage_threshold_high, health_regeneration_rate).

questions.q: Could this be decomposed further? Into what?
questions.a: Could split O2 management and temperature management into separate sub-rungs, but the SuitLifeSupportComponent already handles both as one system.

questions.q: At what resolution does the pattern emerge?
questions.a: Pattern emerges after 2-3 O2 cycles (drain → warning → shelter recharge → drain). Player learns the rhythm of 20 minutes exploration / 5 minutes shelter.

questions.q: What would 'deep enough' look like for this feature?
questions.a: When O2 drain + temperature damage create a tension curve: first 5min are safe, 5-15min are manageable, 15-20min are urgent. Player always feels they can make it back to shelter but must respect the clock.

questions.q: What element catalog variables does this train?
questions.a: o2_drain_rate_Lps, o2_tank_capacity_L, temp_hazard_min_C, temp_hazard_max_C, regen_hp_per_sec.

questions.q: How many relevant elements exist in the catalog?
questions.a: 23 catalog entries tagged 'survival' and 'life_support'.

questions.q: Are there enough variables to train meaningfully?
questions.a: Yes — 5 parameters with 23 catalog elements is well-matched for a single-rung training run.

questions.q: What variables are MISSING from the catalog?
questions.a: Biome-specific O2 efficiency (desert heat should drain more O2 than arctic cold due to cooling system overhead).

questions.q: Would training this require GPU acceleration?
questions.a: No — 5 parameters is far below the 1000-variable GPU threshold.

questions.q: Does this feature connect to the Mirror of Erised?
questions.a: Directly — survival pressure IS the cost that gives giving its weight. Without the risk of death, giving costs nothing.

questions.q: How directly does it serve the Mirror? (direct/enabling/orthogonal)
questions.a: Direct — survival creates the scarcity that makes resource sharing meaningful. No body_survival = no reason to give.

questions.q: Would a costless life still be meaningful without this feature?
questions.a: No — body_survival is the foundational cost that makes every other choice consequential. Without it, the player has no skin in the game.

questions.q: Could this feature be gamed to fake a generous life?
questions.a: No — O2 drain and temperature are physiological, not transactional. The player cannot manipulate them to appear generous.

questions.q: What would this feature look like if it perfectly served the Mirror?
questions.a: The player feels their O2 as a live countdown. When they give a resource to an NPC, they feel the cost of the time they spent gathering it. The Mirror glows brighter because the gift cost something real.

questions.q: What other features does this compose with?
questions.a: shelter_threshold (recharges O2, temp safety), biome_resources (hazard rate per biome), beacon_narrative (survival state affects signal rate).

questions.q: What could break at the seam between this and its neighbors?
questions.a: Shelter O2 recharge rate could be slower than outside drain rate — player enters shelter to recharge but loses O2 faster than they gain it. Net negative cycle.

questions.q: Does this need a decoder step to place in the level?
questions.a: No — SuitLifeSupportComponent is a component on BP_Astronaut_Character. Parameters are set on the character blueprint.

questions.q: What would a failed composition look like?
questions.a: Composition test with body_survival (5 params) + shelter_threshold (4 params) creates an O2 loop where shelter recharge < open-world drain rate. Player cannot survive even with optimal shelter use.

questions.q: Does this feature need a human judgment or can the system verify it?
questions.a: System verifies drain rates and thresholds with precise measurement. Human judges whether the tension curve feels like 'fun urgency' vs 'panic stress.'

questions.q: How many generations to converge?
questions.a: ~100 generations at pop=128 for 5-parameter survival curve optimization. Already trained to score 1.0.

questions.q: What population size is appropriate?
questions.a: 128 — survival curves need diverse genome exploration to find the tension sweet spot.

questions.q: What's the risk of overfitting?
questions.a: Medium — a winner tuned for a specific terrain size and shelter density may fail with different level scales.

questions.q: What's the risk of underfitting?
questions.a: Low — 5 parameters with clear walls (min/max drain rates, capacity floor) produce workable solutions in a wide band.

questions.q: Does the existing trainer support this domain type?
questions.a: Yes — core.trainer was used to train this rung. The Python simulation evaluates O2 curves against the objective.

questions.q: Have we gone deep enough on this feature?
questions.a: Yes — the rung is trained, decoded, and working. Additional depth would be biome-specific O2 modifiers (sub-rungs).

questions.q: What would the NEXT level of decomposition look like?
questions.a: Per-biome O2 efficiency: desert O2 drain 1.3x, arctic O2 drain 0.8x, with independent training per biome type.

questions.q: If we stopped here, the game feel complete?
questions.a: Yes — the survival loop works. Body_survival is one of the first trained and decoded rungs.

questions.q: What is the human's expected emotional response to this feature?
questions.a: Urgency with a safety net — the O2 warning creates focused gameplay without punishing mistakes too harshly. The player becomes a better explorer by learning to respect the tank.

questions.q: Does this feature exist because the Mirror demands it, or because it's technically interesting?
questions.a: The Mirror demands it — survival pressure is the non-negotiable foundation for meaningful cost. No body_survival, no sacrifice, no Mirror.
